section.title: Keystores
section.para: A Keystore is required by a Port in order to use SSL for messaging and/or management.
The Broker supports a number of different keystore types. These are described below.

The key material may be held by the Broker itself (held inline within the configuration) or you may use references to files on the server's file system. Whichever mechanism is chosen it is imperative to ensure that private key material remains confidential.

section.title: Types
section.para:
The following keystore types are supported.
File Key Store. This type accepts the standard JKS keystore format undertood by Java and Java tools such as keytool.
If the keystore contains multiple keys, it is possible to indicate which certificate is to be used by specifying an alias. If no alias is specified the first certificate found in the keystore will be used.
Non Java Key Store. A Non Java Keystore accepts key material in PEM and DER file formats. With this store type it is necessary to provide the private key, which must not be protected by password, certificate and optionally a file containing intermediate certificates.
Auto Generated Self Signed has the ability to generate a self signed certificate and produce a truststore suitable for use by an application using the Apache Qpid JMS and Apache Qpid JMS AMQP 0-x clients.
The use of self signed certficates is not recommended for production use.
Generating the certificate requires a certificate generator, see . A keystore whose certificate has already been generated loads without one.

section.title: Attributes

listitem.para: Name the keystore. Used to identify the keystore.

section.para: The following attributes apply to File Key Stores only.

listitem.para: Keystore path. File Key Stores only. Path to keystore file

Keystore password. Password used to secure the keystore
The password of the certificate used by the Broker must match the password of the keystore itself. This is a restriction of the Broker implementation. If using the keytool utility, note that this means the argument to the -keypass option must match the -storepass option.
Certificate Alias. An optional way of specifying which certificate the broker should use if the keystore contains multiple entries.
Manager Factory Algorithm.In keystores the have more than one certificate, the alias identifies the certificate to be used.
Key Store Type. Type of Keystore.

Use SNI host name matching. If selected, SNI server name from an SSL handshake will be used to select the most appropriate certificate by matching an indicated hostname with the certificate hostname specified in subject or subject alternatives as CN or DC.

section.para: The following attributes apply to Non Java Key Stores only.

listitem.para: Private Key. The private key in DER or PEM format. This file must not be password protected.
Certificate. The cerificate in DER or PEM format.
Intermediates Certificates . Optional. Intermediate cerificates in PEM or DER format.

section.para: The following attributes apply to Auto Generated Self Signed only.

listitem.para: Algorithm. Optional. Algorithm used to generate the self-signed certificate.
Signature Algorithm . Optional. The name of signature algorithm.
Key Length. Optional. Length of the key in bits.
Duration. Optional. Validility period in months.

section.title: Certificate Generators
section.para: Auto Generated Self Signed keystores use a certificate generator to build their certificate. The Broker distribution includes one, the qpid-broker-plugins-certificate-generator-bouncycastle plugin (type BouncyCastle), which uses the Bouncy Castle PKIX library to assemble and encode the certificate. Key pair generation and signing use the Java security providers configured in the JVM; the plugin does not register any security provider.

If no certificate generator is installed, the Auto Generated Self Signed type remains available and existing keystores of this type continue to work, but creating a keystore or regenerating its certificate fails. Applications that embed the Broker and depend on qpid-broker-core directly need to add the plugin and the Bouncy Castle libraries bcprov-jdk18on, bcpkix-jdk18on and bcutil-jdk18on to keep this functionality.
The Broker selects the certificate generator at startup:

listitem.para: If the system property qpid.security.certificateGenerator (see ) is set, the generator of that type is used. The Broker fails to start if that type is not installed or its generator cannot be created.
Otherwise, if several certificate generators are installed, the Broker fails to start; set the property to choose one.

section.para: An installed certificate generator can be disabled with the system property qpid.plugin.disabled:certificategeneratorfactory.<type> set to true, for example qpid.plugin.disabled:certificategeneratorfactory.BouncyCastle.

Production deployments should use certificates issued by a certificate authority, supplied through a File Key Store or a Non Java Key Store. Such keys and certificates can be created with tools such as keytool or openssl and do not require a certificate generator.

section.title: Writing your own certificate generator
section.para: A certificate generator is a Broker plugin implementing the org.apache.qpid.server.security.certificate.CertificateGeneratorFactory interface and annotated with @PluggableService. The factory has a public no-argument constructor without side effects, and returns a unique type from getType(). Its create() method returns a CertificateGenerator, which builds a self-signed X.509 version 3 certificate from a CertificateRequest.

Generators should use the default Java security provider selection and must not register security providers. The abstract test org.apache.qpid.server.security.certificate.AbstractCertificateGeneratorContractTest, in the qpid-broker-core test jar, checks that a generator meets this contract: the certificate is a self-signed X.509 version 3 certificate for the generated key pair with the requested algorithms, key length, subject and validity period, a positive and unique serial number, a critical basic constraints extension marking it as an end entity, and a non-critical subject alternative name extension holding the DNS names and IP addresses of the request (left out when there are none); the JCA standard signature algorithm names are accepted, unknown key and signature algorithm names are reported as NoSuchAlgorithmException, and no security provider is registered. A generator may add further extensions, and may accept further signature algorithm names; keystores configured with such a name may not work with other generators.
